sections.h2: What are the options for selling a house in St. Joseph, MO?
sections.html:
Owners in St. Joseph can work with an agent, skip the agent, or accept an as-is bid from a cash buyer. The best fit depends on the house's condition, your deadline, and what the local market will pay.

Local prices stand apart from the other cities in this series. The 2020 to 2024 survey puts the middle home value here at $154,200, against $197,500 in St. Louis city and $298,700 in St. Charles. When the price is lower, a few thousand dollars of repairs or fees takes a bigger share of what you keep, so it pays to work out a net figure for each route.

  • Agent sale: wide exposure, with fees and timing set by the listing contract and the buyer's lender.
  • Owner sale: cheaper, though marketing and paperwork are yours.
  • Cash sale: the buyer accepts the house with its flaws, and the closing day is negotiable.

sections.h2: What kind of city is St. Joseph for a home seller?
sections.html:
St. Joseph is the seat of Buchanan County, on the Missouri River in the northwest corner of the state, about 30 miles north of Kansas City. Joseph Robidoux, a fur trader, founded it, and it was incorporated in 1843. Wikipedia says it was the westernmost point reachable by rail until after the Civil War, and that it was an endpoint of the Pony Express from April 1860 to late October 1861. Outlaw Jesse James died here, and the city's slogan reflects both.

The downtown grid carries the names of Robidoux's children, including Faraon, Jules, Francois, Felix, Edmond, Charles, Sylvanie and Messanie. The city covers 44.04 square miles of land and has a 26-mile parkway system with an urban trail, anchored by Krug Park on the north and Hyde Park on the south. Corby Pond, Lake Contrary and the riverwalk add to the outdoor options.

Population has slipped slowly: the Census Bureau puts the mid-2025 estimate at 71,001, down 2.0% from the 2020 base.

sections.h2: What work and schools keep buyers in St. Joseph?
sections.html:
Manufacturing and health care anchor the local economy. According to Wikipedia, St. Joseph has the third-largest manufacturing economy in Missouri, after St. Louis and Kansas City. A 2019 list of employers names Mosaic Life Care at 2,922 workers, Triumph Foods at 2,400, the St. Joseph School District at 1,635, the 139th Airlift Wing of the Missouri Air National Guard at 1,114, and Boehringer Ingelheim Vetmedica at 1,070.

Most of the city lies in the St. Joseph School District, which operates three public high schools (Benton, Central and Lafayette), four middle schools and 16 elementary schools. A small piece of the city belongs to the Mid-Buchanan County R-V School District. Shopping is concentrated along North Belt Highway on the east side, including East Hills Mall, and two interstates, I-29 and I-229, connect the city to Kansas City and Council Bluffs. Wikipedia notes that the downtown portion of I-229 is slated to be demolished and replaced with a surface boulevard, so ask the city about plans if your house sits near that corridor.

sections.h2: Does St. Joseph have rules for rental houses and inspections?
sections.html:
Yes. The city runs a Residential Rental Certification Program that began in July 2019 and requires rental units to pass a minimum code inspection every five years. If the house you are selling is a rental, the certification matters to a buyer who plans to keep it rented.

The city's application materials list an inspection fee of $50.00 for each inspection performed by a city inspector, and rentals also need a business license. Forms go to the Housing Compliance Inspection Office, 1100 Frederick Avenue, City Hall Room 107.

  • Business license for rental units: online application.
  • Unit Certification Application and Consent of Entry forms.
  • Residential Rental Unit Inspection Checklist, which shows what inspectors look for on the exterior and interior.
  • Tenant Complaint Form, useful to know about if a tenant has raised concerns.

Ask the Housing Compliance office whether your address has a current certificate before you list or sign a contract. For an owner-occupied house, call the same office to ask whether any inspection applies to your parcel before closing.

sections.html:
Home values and rents here are the lowest of the four cities in this series, and the poverty rate is high. The table gathers the main QuickFacts numbers.

sections.h2: Where do you record a deed in Buchanan County?
sections.html:
Deeds for St. Joseph property are recorded with the Buchanan County Recorder of Deeds at 411 Jules Street, Room 103, St. Joseph, MO 64501. Visits run Monday through Friday, opening at eight in the morning and closing at half past four, and the phone is 816-271-1437. The recorder's stated policy is that nothing is recorded after 4:00 p.m.; papers handed in later are recorded in the order received when the next business day starts at 8:00 a.m.

The recorder says it cannot draw up deeds or answer legal questions and recommends retaining an attorney or title company. Call the office for current fees, because the amount depends on the document. Any recording charge will show on your settlement statement.

sections.h2: What conveniences can a St. Joseph seller point to?
sections.html:
Buyers who commute or travel will ask about access. St. Joseph Transit, which is publicly owned, runs bus service in town, and Jefferson Lines provides intercity buses. Rosecrans Memorial Airport serves general aviation and the 139th Airlift Wing but has no commercial flights, so the nearest airline airport is Kansas City International, about 35 miles south.

Within the city, the four-branch public library system, the Pony Express Museum in the former company stables and the Missouri Theater are part of the draw, and Missouri Western State University adds a student population of more than 3,800.

sections.h2: How do river and weather conditions affect St. Joseph houses?
sections.html:
Wikipedia describes a humid subtropical climate bordering on humid continental, with nearby stations typically reporting 12 to 20 inches of snow a year. The airport sits low, near the Missouri River, and its winter lows run several degrees colder than elsewhere in the city. Streams and water bodies include Roys Branch, Whitehead Creek and the river itself.

If your house is near a creek or the river, gather any elevation certificate, flood insurance records and repair receipts for your buyer. Asking neighbors and the city about drainage problems before you list helps you answer questions truthfully, whether your buyer is financing or paying cash.

faqs.q: How high are home values in St. Joseph?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 survey gives $154,200 for a typical owned home. Median gross rent is $898.

faqs.q: Which office handles a deed for a St. Joseph sale?
faqs.a: The Buchanan County Recorder of Deeds, 411 Jules Street, Room 103, phone 816-271-1437. Nothing is recorded after 4:00 p.m., so a late-day filing is recorded the next business day.

faqs.q: Are St. Joseph rental houses inspected?
faqs.a: Yes. Under the Residential Rental Certification Program, begun in July 2019, rental units must pass a minimum code inspection every five years, and the application lists a $50.00 fee for each city inspection.

faqs.q: Which school district covers most of St. Joseph?
faqs.a: The St. Joseph School District, with Benton, Central and Lafayette high schools. A small piece of the city is in the Mid-Buchanan County R-V district.

faqs.q: Can a St. Joseph house in rough shape be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. It can be listed, sold by the owner, or sold as-is to a cash buyer. For a rental, ask the Housing Compliance Inspection Office at City Hall about its certification status.
